headline: Cheng Ping, chair of Delta Electronics, a Taiwanese power equipment maker, warns that electricity supply may not keep up with AI data center growth.
score_reason: A forecast from an interested company; figures are estimates he cited.
importance_line: Households and businesses could face tighter power supply, data center builders may be slowed, and Delta sells power equipment, so the warning also serves its interests.
source: Taiwan News, citing CNA and Anue
summary: Taiwan News reports, citing CNA, that Delta Electronics chair Cheng Ping said on Thursday that power infrastructure is not keeping pace with AI data centers, citing estimates that US data centers will add 44 gigawatts of demand by 2028 while the grid adds only 25 gigawatts. Delta, a maker of power equipment, is itself investing in fuel cells and new transformers, so the warning comes from a company with a stake in the answer.
notes: Delta is a power equipment maker; interested party.
